hints: Focus on what functional groups are present in carvone and what type of reagent $\text{NaBH}_4$ is.
Remember that $\text{NaBH}_4$ reduces carbonyls like ketones to alcohols but leaves $\text{C=C}$ double bonds untouched.
Look for the structure where only the $\text{C=O}$ has become $\text{CH-OH}$ while both alkene bonds are still there.
walkthrough:
**Spot the functional groups in carvone**

Look carefully at carvone. It has three reactive sites: one ketone $\text{C=O}$ and two different $\text{C=C}$ alkenes, one in the ring and one in the side chain.

Carvone = cyclic $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone + isolated alkene

**Recall what NaBH4 does**

$\text{NaBH}_4$ is a selective reducing agent. It is a source of hydride, $\text{H}^-$, that attacks the carbonyl carbon.

$$\text{R}_2\text{C=O} \xrightarrow{\text{NaBH}_4} \text{R}_2\text{CH-OH}$$
It reduces aldehydes to primary alcohols and ketones to secondary alcohols, but it does NOT reduce $\text{C=C}$ bonds.

**Apply selectivity to carvone**

So only the ketone changes. The $\text{C=O}$ becomes $\text{CH-OH}$, a secondary alcohol. Both the ring $\text{C=C}$ and the exocyclic $\text{C=C}$ stay exactly as they are. That matches only one of the four structures.

options.A: Correct. The ketone $\text{C=O}$ has been reduced to a secondary alcohol $\text{CH-OH}$, while both $\text{C=C}$ bonds (ring alkene and side-chain $\text{C(CH}_3\text{)=CH}_2$) are unchanged. This is exactly the chemoselectivity of $\text{NaBH}_4$.
options.B: Incorrect. This structure keeps the ketone but has reduced both $\text{C=C}$ bonds. $\text{NaBH}_4$ does the opposite, it reduces $\text{C=O}$ and leaves $\text{C=C}$ alone. This looks like the product of catalytic hydrogenation with $\text{H}_2$ / Ni, not $\text{NaBH}_4$.
options.C: Incorrect. This structure keeps the ketone $\text{C=O}$ and reduces only the side-chain alkene to an isopropyl group. $\text{NaBH}_4$ does not reduce isolated alkenes, so the $\text{C=O}$ should have reacted, not the alkene.
options.D: Incorrect. Although the ketone has correctly become an alcohol, both $\text{C=C}$ bonds have also been reduced to single bonds. $\text{NaBH}_4$ is not strong enough to reduce alkenes, so this over-reduced product cannot form.
